title: Phoenix EDR / single-frame RDR filename
reference: Phoenix Camera EDR / RDR Data Products SIS (JPL D-33231, PHX-274-327), §4.4.1

segments.label: Instrument
segments.description: Phoenix instrument that acquired the data.

values.A: Robotic Arm (not a camera; not described by the camera SIS)
values.E: Entry science (not described by the camera SIS)
values.F: MECA Atomic Force Microscope (not described by the camera SIS)
values.L: MET LIDAR (not described by the camera SIS)
values.M: MET pressure and temperature (not described by the camera SIS)
values.P: MECA Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe (not described by the camera SIS)
values.T: Thermal and Evolved Gas Analyzer (not described by the camera SIS)
values.W: MECA Wet Chemistry (not described by the camera SIS)
values.X: MECA miscellaneous (not described by the camera SIS)

segments.label: Epoch
segments.description: Which model and mission phase the data came from.

segments.label: Sol
segments.description: Martian solar day of the observation.

patterns.meaning: Sol {number} on the surface (landing day is sol 1), or day of year if the epoch is cruise or testbed

segments.label: Product type
segments.description: What the product holds. A leading "E" marks an EDR; on an RDR a trailing "L" marks a linearized (distortion-removed) product.

EFF.description: EDRs are raw: no camera model linearization and no radiometric correction. SIS §5.1.

ESF.description: EDRs are raw: no camera model linearization and no radiometric correction. SIS §5.1.

EDN.description: EDRs are raw: no camera model linearization and no radiometric correction. SIS §5.1.

EDK.description: EDRs are raw: no camera model linearization and no radiometric correction. SIS §5.1.

ERP.description: EDRs are raw: no camera model linearization and no radiometric correction. SIS §5.1.

FFL.description: Geometrically corrected RDRs repeat the EDR pixels with the camera distortion removed, so stereo geometry is linear. SIS §5.2.1.1. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

SFL.description: Geometrically corrected RDRs repeat the EDR pixels with the camera distortion removed, so stereo geometry is linear. SIS §5.2.1.1. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

DNL.description: Geometrically corrected RDRs repeat the EDR pixels with the camera distortion removed, so stereo geometry is linear. SIS §5.2.1.1. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

RAD.meaning: Radiometric — Radiometrically corrected to absolute radiance units
RAD.description: Radiometrically corrected RDRs convert raw DN into physical units, correcting for instrument response, exposure and flat field. SIS §5.2.1.2.

RAL.meaning: Radiometric — Radiometrically corrected to absolute radiance units, linearized
RAL.description: Radiometrically corrected RDRs convert raw DN into physical units, correcting for instrument response, exposure and flat field. SIS §5.2.1.2. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

RSD.description: Radiometrically corrected RDRs convert raw DN into physical units, correcting for instrument response, exposure and flat field. SIS §5.2.1.2.

RSL.meaning: Radiometric — Radiometrically corrected, contrast enhanced, linearized
RSL.description: Radiometrically corrected RDRs convert raw DN into physical units, correcting for instrument response, exposure and flat field. SIS §5.2.1.2. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

IOF.meaning: Radiometric — Radiometrically corrected to I/F radiance factor
IOF.description: Radiometrically corrected RDRs convert raw DN into physical units, correcting for instrument response, exposure and flat field. SIS §5.2.1.2.

IOL.meaning: Radiometric — Radiometrically corrected to I/F radiance factor, linearized
IOL.description: Radiometrically corrected RDRs convert raw DN into physical units, correcting for instrument response, exposure and flat field. SIS §5.2.1.2. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

DIS.description: Disparity RDRs hold the stereo parallax in pixels between a point in one eye and its match in the other, the input to the XYZ products. SIS §5.2.1.3.

DIL.description: Disparity RDRs hold the stereo parallax in pixels between a point in one eye and its match in the other, the input to the XYZ products. SIS §5.2.1.3. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

DSS.description: Disparity RDRs hold the stereo parallax in pixels between a point in one eye and its match in the other, the input to the XYZ products. SIS §5.2.1.3.

DSL.meaning: Disparity — Stereo disparity of samples, linearized
DSL.description: Disparity RDRs hold the stereo parallax in pixels between a point in one eye and its match in the other, the input to the XYZ products. SIS §5.2.1.3. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

DLS.description: Disparity RDRs hold the stereo parallax in pixels between a point in one eye and its match in the other, the input to the XYZ products. SIS §5.2.1.3.

DLL.meaning: Disparity — Stereo disparity of lines, linearized
DLL.description: Disparity RDRs hold the stereo parallax in pixels between a point in one eye and its match in the other, the input to the XYZ products. SIS §5.2.1.3. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

XYZ.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4.

XYL.meaning: XYZ — XYZ position per pixel, linearized
XYL.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

MSK.meaning: Mask — XYZ lander volume exclusion mask
MSK.description: Mask files flag which pixels of a companion product are valid or excluded because lander hardware fills them. SIS §5.2.1.4.

MSL.meaning: Mask — XYZ lander volume exclusion mask, linearized
MSL.description: Mask files flag which pixels of a companion product are valid or excluded because lander hardware fills them. SIS §5.2.1.4. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

XMZ.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4.

XML.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

XXX.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4.

XXL.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

YYY.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4.

YYL.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

ZZZ.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4.

ZZL.description: XYZ RDRs give each pixel a three-dimensional position in a Phoenix coordinate frame, so the workspace can be measured. SIS §5.2.1.4. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

RNG.description: Range RDRs give the distance from the camera to the surface at each pixel. SIS §5.2.1.5.

RNL.meaning: Range — Range (distance from the camera), linearized
RNL.description: Range RDRs give the distance from the camera to the surface at each pixel. SIS §5.2.1.5. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

UVW.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6.

UVL.meaning: Surface normal — UVW surface normal, linearized
UVL.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

UUU.meaning: Surface normal — Surface normal U component
UUU.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6.

UUL.meaning: Surface normal — Surface normal U component, linearized
UUL.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

VVV.meaning: Surface normal — Surface normal V component
VVV.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6.

VVL.meaning: Surface normal — Surface normal V component, linearized
VVL.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

WWW.meaning: Surface normal — Surface normal W component
WWW.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6.

WWL.meaning: Surface normal — Surface normal W component, linearized
WWL.description: Surface Normal (UVW) RDRs give the unit normal of the terrain at each pixel, the basis for slope and roughness. SIS §5.2.1.6. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

RUF.description: Roughness RDRs measure how far the terrain departs from a plane. SIS §5.2.1.7.

RUL.description: Roughness RDRs measure how far the terrain departs from a plane. SIS §5.2.1.7. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

SLP.description: Slope RDRs derive terrain steepness, heading and magnitude from the surface normals. SIS §5.2.1.8.

SLL.description: Slope RDRs derive terrain steepness, heading and magnitude from the surface normals. SIS §5.2.1.8. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

SHP.description: Slope RDRs derive terrain steepness, heading and magnitude from the surface normals. SIS §5.2.1.8.

SHL.description: Slope RDRs derive terrain steepness, heading and magnitude from the surface normals. SIS §5.2.1.8. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

SMP.description: Slope RDRs derive terrain steepness, heading and magnitude from the surface normals. SIS §5.2.1.8.

SML.description: Slope RDRs derive terrain steepness, heading and magnitude from the surface normals. SIS §5.2.1.8. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

IDD.description: Reachability RDRs mark which terrain the Robotic Arm can reach — the products that drove Phoenix's digging. SIS §5.2.1.9.

IDL.description: Reachability RDRs mark which terrain the Robotic Arm can reach — the products that drove Phoenix's digging. SIS §5.2.1.9. A trailing "L" on an RDR code means the product is linearized.

segments.label: Spacecraft clock
segments.description: Spacecraft clock count at the start of the camera event.

patterns.meaning: Special processing "{value}" — an off-nominal treatment used consistently within one activity and listed in the archive's special-processing text file

segments.label: Activity ID
segments.description: Planned activity the observation belongs to, taken from the round-trip accountability token.

patterns.meaning: Activity "{value}", assigned at planning time and carried in the round-trip accountability token

segments.label: Payload flag
segments.description: Four bits of the accountability token describing the observation: mosaic or not, stereo or not, and its purpose.

values.0: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, non-stereo (general science). Optical Microscope: single frame, single focus, monochrome (clean)
values.1: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, non-stereo (calibration). Optical Microscope: single frame, single focus, monochrome (exposed)
values.2: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, non-stereo, mesh or reachability (operations). Optical Microscope: single frame, single focus, colour (clean)
values.3: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, non-stereo (atmospheric). Optical Microscope: single frame, single focus, colour (exposed)
values.4: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, stereo (general science). Optical Microscope: single frame, through focus, monochrome (clean)
values.5: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, stereo (calibration). Optical Microscope: single frame, through focus, monochrome (exposed)
values.6: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, stereo, mesh or reachability (operations). Optical Microscope: single frame, through focus, colour (clean)
values.7: SSI / RAC: non-mosaic, stereo (atmospheric). Optical Microscope: single frame, through focus, colour (exposed)
values.8: SSI / RAC: mosaic, non-stereo (general science). Optical Microscope: mosaic, single focus, monochrome (clean)
values.9: SSI / RAC: mosaic, non-stereo (calibration). Optical Microscope: mosaic, single focus, monochrome (exposed)
values.A: SSI / RAC: mosaic, non-stereo, mesh or reachability (operations). Optical Microscope: mosaic, single focus, colour (clean)
values.B: SSI / RAC: mosaic, non-stereo (atmospheric). Optical Microscope: mosaic, single focus, colour (exposed)
values.C: SSI / RAC: mosaic, stereo (general science). Optical Microscope: mosaic, through focus, monochrome (clean)
values.D: SSI / RAC: mosaic, stereo (calibration). Optical Microscope: mosaic, through focus, monochrome (exposed)
values.E: SSI / RAC: mosaic, stereo, mesh or reachability (operations). Optical Microscope: mosaic, through focus, colour (clean)
values.F: SSI / RAC: mosaic, stereo (atmospheric). Optical Microscope: mosaic, through focus, colour (exposed)

segments.label: Camera eye
segments.description: Which eye the image came from.

values.A: Anaglyph — left, right and right eyes mapped to red, green and blue

segments.label: Filter / LED
segments.description: SSI spectral filter position, or which LED lit the RAC or Optical Microscope frame.

segments.label: Version
segments.description: Increments whenever an otherwise identical filename would be produced, independently of the special processing field, so the highest version is the best copy.

values.IMG: Image EDR / RDR with a PDS label
values.RGB: Terrain mesh skin in SGI RGB format
